name: Bieten
description: Bieten (German: 'Bidding' or 'Offering') is a highly unusual gambling game from the Austrian Tyrol played with a 33-card German-suited pack including the iconic WELI wild card. Each player receives only 3 cards, and points are scored for having the best Heart card, the best Leaf card, the best pair/triple, the best sequence, and winning the last trick. Players can 'Bieten' (bet) on any of these categories, escalating the stakes, or their opponents can concede the point. It is essentially a multi-dimensional bluffing game.

history.origins: Rooted deeply in the Austrian Tyrol and Bavarian card-game tradition. The WELI card is a hallmark of Tyrolean card games. Bieten draws on the same tradition as Watten and Schnapsen.
timeline: Present: Still played actively in Tyrol, Bavaria, and South Tyrol, especially in mountain communities.
history.cultural: The WELI card is unique to this region. In Bieten, it acts as a wild card and can represent any card.
history.evolution: The game's core innovation is its multi-point structure. Unlike most games where ONE thing wins, Bieten has FIVE simultaneous point categories, each bettable independently.

setup.deck: 33-card German-suited pack: A, K, Over (O), Under (U), 10, 9, 8, 7 in 4 suits (Hearts/Rot, Leaves/GrÃ¼n, Bells/Schellen, Acorns/Eichel) + WELI (special 6 of Bells wild card).
setup.dealing: Deal 3 cards to each player. No trump is established. No kitty.

rules.objective: Score the most points across 5 categories: Best Heart (Rot), Best Leaf (GrÃ¼n), Best Pair/Triple (Gleich), Best Sequence (Hanger), and the Last Trick (Spiel).
rules.gameplay: Starting with best hand, players may 'Bieten' (bet) on any category they wish to contest. Any opposing player can either: Concede (auto-lose the category, worth its base value) OR Call (match the bet, escalating the point value). At showdown, the best hand wins the doubled/escalated value.
keyRules: WELI is wild: its owner declares what card it represents.
A player may bet on a category they cannot possibly win as a bluff.
Game targets a fixed score (e.g., 15 points).

strategy.basic: Don't Bieten a category you can't win unless you're willing to bluff. With 3 cards, information is scarce.
strategy.intermediate: The WELI allows creative bluffs. If you hold WELI + a middling card, you can Bieten for Best Heart claiming your WELI is the Ace of Hearts. Opponents don't know!
strategy.advanced: Multi-Category Hands: A hand with a pair AND a high heart is extremely powerful. Bieten on multiple fronts forces opponents to spend concessions.
tips: Conceding is not weaknessâ€”if the bet is small and your card is weak, save your chips.
The Last Trick (Spiel) is a guaranteed category for the player holding the highest card in the last suit led.

variations.name: Weli as Fixed Bonus
variations.description: Weli is not wild; instead its holder scores a bonus point automatically.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variant only changes how Weli scores; the engine structure and phases remain the same.

variations.name: Triple Wild Variant
variations.description: WELI, 7 of Bells, and 7 of Acorns are all wild. All rank below the real cards they represent.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variant only changes which cards are wild; engine configuration and progression do not need overrides.

scoring.description: Each category is worth 1 base point (or more if contested/bet up).

synthesis.shortDescription: A rare bluffing masterpiece from the Austrian Alps. With only 3 cards, you compete on 5 distinct categories simultaneouslyâ€”and a single wild WELI card can win any of them. Bold betting is everything.
